newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks close higher on ADRs' coat-tails.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks close higher on ADRs' coat-tails.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed higher on Tuesday, pushed up by increases in New York-listed ADRs and bouyant "Chispa" investment companies' shares, traders said.
The 40-stock IPSA index rose 0.75 percent to end at 132.23 points as turnover more than doubled from Monday's session to 16.9 billion pesos (about $40.7 million). Advances led declines 62 to 41.
Traders said they expected to see renewed foreign interest in Chilean stocks on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve left U.S. interest rates unchanged.
Among the session's winners was Compania Cervecerias Unidas, up 4.55 percent after Smith Barney analysts raised their rating for the brewers to outperform from neutral.
Other gainers were among the so-called Chispas, a group of investment firms that control a major stake in electricity holding company Enersis .
Spanish utility Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa-Espana) this week opened a tender to buy Chispa shares.
Endesa-Espana's brokers, Santander Investment, said on Tuesday that they would open a special tender at local bourse to purchase shares in Compania de Inversiones Luz, one of the Chispas.
Four Chilean pension funds hold Luz shares but were restricted from taking part in the over-the-counter tender.
After Santander's announcement, Luz series A shares closed up six percent.
